newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Parkway to restructure Indonesia holdings.
newsitem.headline: Parkway to restructure Indonesia holdings.

text.p: Healthcare company Parkway Holdings Ltd said on Monday it planned to restructure its Indonesian healthcare projects into one corporate vehicle, PT Siloam Gleneagles Health Care (Siloam).
Parkway said in a statement the restructuring would enable it to more fully capitalise on market opportunities.
No financial details of the proposed deal were disclosed.
Parkway said restructuring would impact existing projects and it was in discussions with its partners in the Medan Hospital and the Budi Mulia Hospital to explain the effects.
Parkway had an existing partnership with Siloam to build the Siloam Gleneagles Hospital.

The proposed restructuring, subject to regulatory approval, would involve the divestment by Gleneagles Development Pte Ltd (GDPL), a Parkway unit, of its interests in the Budi Mulia and Medan projects to Siloam.

The Parkway statement said Siloam would fund the acquisition through the issue of 47 million new shares. GDPL, which currently owns 30 percent of Siloam, would see its stake diluted to 20.39 percent as a result, the statement said.
